documents.title: Operative hysteroscopy with lysis of adhesions
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Date of surgery: 01/19/2023
Preoperative diagnosis: Asherman syndrome, secondary amenorrhea.
Postoperative diagnosis: intrauterine adhesions.
Procedure: operative hysteroscopy with lysis of intrauterine adhesions.
Anesthesia: general (LMA).

Findings: cervix dilated without difficulty. Adhesions within the uterine cavity, divided sharply with hysteroscopic scissors. At the end of the procedure the cavity had a normal contour.
Fluid deficit and blood loss minimal. No complications.

Disposition: discharged home from recovery. Office follow-up in 6 weeks; nothing in the vagina for 2 weeks. Call for fever, heavy bleeding or worsening pain.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up after hysteroscopy
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Visit date: 03/07/2023

Seen 7 weeks after hysteroscopic adhesiolysis. Her periods have returned, two cycles so far, with flow she describes as back to what she had before the D&C and much less cramping. No fever or discharge after surgery.

Exam: abdomen benign, uterus normal size and nontender.

Assessment: Asherman syndrome, treated; menses restored.

Plan: no restriction on trying to conceive from here. Early prenatal care once pregnant. Next cervical co-test June 2023. Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

reports.text:
Liquid-based cytology. Satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present.
Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Co-test result letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Dear Ms. Ortiz,

Your Pap test and HPV test from June 13 are both normal. This is your third negative co-test in a row since your LEEP. You can now move to testing every three years. Your next co-test is due in June 2026. Please keep seeing a clinician every year for your general health.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Good news
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Positive test this week!! First day of my last period was June 1. GYN said to call their OB group once it turned positive so I have an intake visit there on the 20th. Do I still come in for my physical in August?

documents.title: RE: Good news
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Wanda! Yes, keep the August physical; it's good for us to see you and it won't duplicate what OB does. In the meantime let your OB know about the D&C and hysteroscopy history at intake (they will probably already have it).

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 33, about 9-10 weeks pregnant (LMP 6/1/23). Intake at the OB group done 7/20 with prenatal labs and a dating scan; she says everything was normal and they will send records.

Interval history: Asherman syndrome diagnosed by GYN in December after the 2021 D&C (amenorrhea, HSG with filling defect, hormones normal). Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis 1/19/23, periods came back normal. Co-test June 2023 negative - third in a row, now every 3 years.

Feels nauseated mornings, keeping food down. No bleeding or cramping.

Meds: none. NKDA.
SH: still teaching, back on 8/28. Partner thrilled. No alcohol, never smoker.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.
PHQ-9 1.

A/P
1. Pregnancy, ~10 wks - care with OB. Flu and COVID vaccines this fall are recommended in pregnancy; Tdap at 27-36 weeks, can do here or at OB.
2. Hx Asherman, treated - OB aware.
3. Hx CIN 3 - next co-test June 2026.
4. No labs today, prenatal panel just done.

RTC 1 yr; will see her for vaccines.

documents.title: OB prenatal summary, first trimester
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Prenatal record summary sent at patient request.

G3P0020, LMP 06/01/2023, EDD 03/07/2024 confirmed by first-trimester ultrasound (single live intrauterine pregnancy, size equals dates).

Prenatal panel 07/20/2023: blood counts normal; rubella immune; hepatitis B surface antigen, HIV and syphilis screens negative; urine culture no growth. Early glucose screen normal. First-trimester genetic screening low risk.

History reviewed: LEEP for CIN 3 2021; septic abortion 2020; D&C for missed abortion 2021; Asherman syndrome treated by hysteroscopy 01/2023; laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2016.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. Blood pressure normal at each visit.
Next: anatomy ultrasound at 20 weeks.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 18 weeks pregnant, feeling well, nausea resolved. No fever. Inactivated quadrivalent influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM R deltoid (preservative-free syringe). Tolerated. Plans to get the updated COVID shot at her pharmacy next week.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization notice
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine 2023-2024 formula, 0.3 mL IM left deltoid, administered 10/12/2023. Patient reported pregnancy, second trimester. No adverse event observed.

documents.title: OB ultrasound, anatomy survey
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Exam date: 10/19/2023. Gestational age 20w0d by dates.
Single live intrauterine pregnancy, cephalic. Fetal biometry consistent with dates. Fetal anatomy survey complete and normal. Placenta posterior fundal, clear of the cervical os. Amniotic fluid normal. Cervical length normal.
Impression: normal anatomy survey.

documents.title: Tdap vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
31w3d by LMP. OB asked that she get Tdap where convenient; came here after school. Feels well, good fetal movement, no headaches, swelling or bleeding. BP and pulse per flowsheet, normal.
Tdap 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated well. Copy faxed to OB.

documents.title: Emergency department physician record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED visit 03/05/2024

CC: headache since yesterday, three days after C-section.

HPI: 33-year-old woman, postpartum day 3 after cesarean delivery under epidural on 3/2, discharged home 3/4. History of CIN 3 (treated) and Asherman syndrome. About 48 hours after surgery she developed a severe, pounding headache across the forehead and the back of the head. It is much worse within minutes of sitting or standing and eases when she lies flat. Nauseated, light hurts her eyes. No fever, no neck pain, no visual loss, no weakness or numbness, no seizure. Breastfeeding.

Meds: ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed from discharge. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: sister had preeclampsia. SH: teacher, no tobacco or alcohol.

Exam: afebrile, vitals within normal limits throughout (see flowsheet). Uncomfortable when sitting up, better supine. Fundi normal bilaterally. Neck supple, no meningismus. No rash. Neurologic exam normal: alert, cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation symmetric, normal gait. Low transverse incision clean and dry. Lungs clear, heart regular. Calves soft.

MDM: classic postural headache after neuraxial anesthesia; blood pressure normal and no neurological findings. Postdural puncture headache. Obstetric anesthesia contacted by phone and agreed with conservative care first.

ED course: 1 L lactated Ringer's IV, acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO and caffeine 300 mg PO. Headache improved lying flat.

Dx: postdural puncture headache.
Dispo: home. Lie flat as much as possible, fluids, caffeinated drinks up to 2-3 a day (fine with breastfeeding at that amount), acetaminophen and ibuprofen as at discharge. Return for fever, stiff neck, confusion, weakness, vision change, or no improvement in 48-72 hours (anesthesia can offer a blood patch). Follow up with primary care this week.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received. Spoke with pt. Headache still there when upright but noticeably less than Tuesday, nausea gone. Staying horizontal as much as she can with her partner home on leave and her mother helping. Afebrile. No stiff neck, no vision change. Feeding and wet diapers fine per pt. Booked video visit with PCP 3/12. Reviewed ED return precautions; she has the anesthesia number if it worsens.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admission 03/02/2024. Discharge 03/04/2024.

G3P0020 at 39w1d. Labor epidural placed for analgesia, then low transverse cesarean delivery under epidural anesthesia on 03/02/2024. Liveborn infant with normal Apgar scores, to well-baby nursery.
Uncomplicated postoperative course. Afebrile; blood pressures normal throughout. Ambulating, tolerating diet, voiding. Breastfeeding established.

Discharge medications: ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed, acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: incision check in 2 weeks; postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: PCP review of delivery records
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed delivery summary and ED record. Uncomplicated cesarean 3/2, then ED 3/5 for postural headache after the epidural, treated conservatively. Video visit 3/12.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for headache

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit; patient at home, baby asleep on her chest for most of it. Identity confirmed, consent for video given.

S: 10 days after cesarean (3/2). Seen in ED 3/5 for a positional headache after the epidural: IV fluids, acetaminophen, caffeine. Headache eased over the next few days and has been completely gone since Sunday, upright or not. No fever, neck stiffness or vision change. Incision fine. Breastfeeding going well, latch good. Sleeping in pieces. Mood "tired but happy"; no intrusive thoughts.
PHQ-9 3.

O: well appearing on video, sitting upright comfortably, speech normal, moves all limbs normally.

A/P
1. Postdural puncture headache - resolved without blood patch.
2. Postpartum, breastfeeding - incision check with OB next week, postpartum visit in April. Discussed when to call about mood.

Annual in August.

documents.title: Postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Visit date 04/12/2024. Six weeks after cesarean delivery.

Recovering well. Postdural puncture headache in the first postpartum week resolved with conservative care. Lochia finished. Exclusively breastfeeding. Mood good; depression screen negative. Blood pressure normal. Weight 70 kg.
Exam: incision well healed. Abdomen soft. Pelvic exam normal.

Plan: routine care. Cervical co-test next due June 2026. Discussed waiting at least 18 months between delivery and the next birth.
Allergies: NKDA. Meds: none.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. 34 as of June. Baby is 5 months, still nursing, starting a bottle at daycare for the fall.

Since last year: cesarean 3/2/24, postdural headache that resolved in a week. Postpartum visit normal.

No complaints. Sleep better now that the baby sleeps 6 hours. Wants to know if her weight is back where it should be - it is close to her pre-pregnancy weight.

Meds: none. NKDA.
SH: back to the classroom later this month. Partner works days. No tobacco or alcohol.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. Neck, thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, low transverse scar healed. No edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 3.

A/P
1. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, A1c (FH diabetes). Flu and COVID in October. Tdap up to date.
2. Hx CIN 3 - co-test June 2026 with GYN.
3. Hx Asherman - no current issues.

RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wanda, all of your labs are normal: no anemia after the delivery, normal kidney and liver tests, normal thyroid, cholesterol fine and A1c normal. See you for flu shot season.

documents.title: We missed you
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Wanda, we missed you for your flu shot appointment yesterday afternoon. No problem at all. You can reply here or call to rebook; nurse visits are open most weekdays after 3.

documents.title: RE: We missed you
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry, daycare pickup ran late and I completely forgot. Can I come Tuesday the 8th after school?

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Trivalent influenza 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Breastfeeding, no contraindication. Tolerated. Pt will get COVID vaccine at pharmacy.

documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: COVID-19 vaccine (Pfizer-BioNTech, 2024-2025 formula) 0.3 mL IM, left deltoid, 10/17/2024. Lot and expiration in pharmacy record. No adverse reaction during observation.

documents.title: Trying again?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick question. We're thinking about trying for a second soon because of my age and how long it took last time. Is there anything I should do first? And can I try a regular delivery next time or am I stuck with a C-section?

documents.title: RE: Trying again?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Good questions. From my side your vaccines are current and your labs in August were all normal.

Whether to try for a vaginal birth after a cesarean is a decision to make with your OB, who knows the details of your surgery; many women can. They will also talk with you about spacing, since a shorter gap between a cesarean and the next delivery carries some extra risk. Worth a call to them before you start trying.
